rationale: Astra makes the most useful delegation boundary concrete: the agent reads logs, a separate reviewed path deploys r42, and the agent’s next direct deployment is still denied. Its larger labels and separated paths are easiest to follow at phone width. Baseline remains useful for schema validity versus authorization, while Fable shows malicious tool output steering the model without gaining execution authority.
findings: Baseline 00:01–00:09 versus 00:11.5–00:18.25: both requests pass schema validation, but only the metrics read is authorized; production remains version 7. This explicitly separates argument validity from authority, which the alternatives leave implicit.

Astra 00:09.5–00:18.5 and 00:21–00:24.1: a reviewed release changes production, then the agent is still denied a direct deployment while its read succeeds. This is the strongest counterexample to approval granting broad agent permissions.

Fable 00:09–00:16.24: an allowed ticket read returns DELETE users, the model follows it despite its prompt rule, and the runtime rejects users.delete. It uniquely shows why permissions must survive a model being misled; it does not imply all injections always succeed.

Legibility at 00:16.5 and 00:20.4: Fable’s revised compact permission-port ripples no longer cross the runtime grant label, and 32px bright sublabels make the prompt/grant distinction clearer. Astra’s 47px actor and 38px state labels remain the easiest of the three at 350px width.

Pacing and endings: baseline’s 24 seconds spend longer on a simpler two-case contrast, including the 00:18.25–00:22.5 outcome hold with a 00:20.5 target pulse. Astra earns its 28 seconds with the post-approval retry; Fable’s 00:19.94 second denial reinforces unchanged grants. All final exact endpoint pairs match, including Fable’s preserved title-only ending.

Boundary of the lesson at Astra 00:12.6–00:18.5 and Fable 00:16.24–00:22: r42 abbreviates an action-bound approval record, and rejection represents an out-of-scope call. The guide supplies identity, artifact/target binding, alternate-path and fail-closed requirements; these animations do not demonstrate credential isolation, replay protection, or an authorization-service outage.
contentVerdict: Keep core, after tool-design and before agents receive shared-system credentials. The guide changes an immediate practice: restrict investigation credentials, bind consequential approval to the exact action, and prove unauthorized requests leave state unchanged. Its definitions, alternate-shell warning, scoped-read caveat, and observable fixture exercise are supported by the five primary documents reviewed on 2026-10-19; the animated architecture remains illustrative.
defectsFixed: Fable: reduced allow/deny port ripples so they do not cross the teaching-critical grant label; enlarged and brightened rule/grant text; retained visibility of the untouched database after denial. Rerendered and regenerated poster.

Fable metadata/transcript: retained original model provenance, added editedBy and corrections metadata, corrected the legitimate-write reference from baseline to astra, and described the title-only ending and visible unchanged database accurately.
Baseline transcript: corrected deployment and denial-response time ranges against the encoded frames; preserved original transcript and left its media unchanged.

Guide: added retrieval dates for the five primary sources actually checked. Local Fable reproduction/verification now caps FFmpeg workers and filters at two and selects the exact final frame by index.
limitations: Audio was analyzed using decoded levels, spectrograms, cue energy, and frame-change alignment; it was not listened to. Subjective loudness, timbre and phone-speaker audibility remain unassessed.
The blind comparison excluded authors’ sources, reviews, scores and provenance until before.md was saved; supplied variant filenames were known, so this was not randomized anonymity.
An initial visual concern about Fable’s loop was disproved by byte-for-byte endpoint comparison. The proposed title fade was reverted and is not reported as a fix.

Frame inspection covers causal beats, busy states, boundaries and endings, with complete automated decoding; it is not human real-time playback or a security implementation audit. No curriculum promotion or publication was performed.
